needsYou.title: Apple Developer Program, or the no-account fallback
needsYou.detail: Nothing to do now. Phases 0-2 and the desktop app don't need it. At phase 3, choose: the paid account (iCloud sync on iOS, no weekly re-install), or the untested fallback where you pick an iCloud Drive folder once and re-install the app every 7 days.

decided.match: How should seqno open a graph
decided.answer: Lazy open: the page list and the visible page load first, the rest fills in behind them.

decided.match: Merge passes by a thin margin
decided.answer: Accepted. Merges run in the worker and never block typing. Verify re-measures on a quiet machine.
The app's own iCloud folder. It shows up as iCloud Drive > seqno in Files and Finder, which matches the plan.
Sync files keep plain ASCII names, and page names get normalized when they're read.

decided.match: How durable should the SQLite index
decided.answer: Relaxed. The index is rebuildable, so it carries a version stamp and rebuilds itself if it ever falls out of sync.

A merge never blocks typing: it runs off the UI thread (web worker now; Loro off the JS thread on iOS in phase 3). 50 ms warm is a target, not a gate. Warm the doc after open and send events only for open pages as tuning.

decided.match: What the 150 MB memory bar measures
decided.answer: Whole process on both platforms. 150 MB is the target until the real-iPhone run sets per-platform numbers. If tight, shallow-snapshot compaction.

decided.match: A device that never comes back
decided.answer: Explicit 'remove this device' setting. A timeout can come later as a prompt, never silently.

carryover: Validate ids before calling Loro: tree.has(undefined|null) crashes inside wasm and the doc is unsafe afterwards.
loro-crdt 1.16.2 web/index.d.ts does not export init: import it from loro-crdt/web/loro_wasm.js; alias loro-crdt to loro-crdt/web so there is one wasm instance.
Import order: import(snapshot) then each update one by one (82 MB WASM); importBatch of everything costs 334 MB.
Vault writes stay off the keystroke path and are batched (real iCloud write p95 37.6 ms on macOS).
Check downloadingStatus before reading a synced file: reading an evicted file silently downloads and blocks ~0.85 s.
Peer and device ids are never reused; a reinstall or backup restore gets a new device id.
Query tests must compare results against an independent oracle (start from spikes/verify/scripts/queries-oracle.ts), not against the same SQL.
SQLite index writes can spike to 70-175 ms; keep them in the worker.
